text:
Olivia Chen: Hi team — external auditor asked for a short sample to validate RBAC changes and accompanying KMS access proofs for a 24h window last month. They want: (1) list of RBAC modifications (who/what/when), (2) signed KMS decrypt/log entries showing key usage, and (3) a checksumed bundle we can hand off. How do we best produce this without leaking unrelated PII?
Samir Patel: Sounds familiar. We usually run a filtered export: RBAC change events from IAM audit logs + Splunk query for KMS CloudTrail events, then package with a manifest and SHA256 of each file.
Maria Gomez: +1. For RBAC diffs I can pull k8s rolebinding change events and our SCIM provisioning logs. Will filter by org_id and time range.
AuditorBot: Please include the change request tickets or PR refs for each change if possible. Auditor needs mapping: change -> approval -> deployment.
Olivia Chen: Good call, include PR/CHG ids. Also need guidance on redaction: remove user emails from logs but keep unique identifiers to show chain of custody. Any recommended approach?
Samir Patel: We redact user emails but keep hashed principal IDs and original timestamps. Example: replace emails with `principal:sha256(<email>)`. That preserves uniqueness without exposing address.
Ethan Park: For KMS access proofs: CloudTrail shows both GenerateDataKey and Decrypt events. We should export the events that reference the key ARN and include the encryptedDataKey logs (no plaintext). The auditor will accept those.
Maria Gomez: Splunk query I plan to run (will share):
```
index=audit source="k8s_audit" OR source="scim" OR source="cloudtrail"
"rolebinding" OR "AddUserToGroup" OR "Decrypt" keyId="arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/"
| where _time >= strptime("2025-01-10T00:00:00Z", "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") AND _time <= strptime("2025-01-11T00:00:00Z", "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
| table _time, event_type, principal, resource, requestParameters, responseElements, requestId
```
Samir Patel: Perfect. After export, we'll: 1) redact emails -> `principal:sha256(...)`, 2) generate SHA256 for each file, 3) sign manifest with the security key (GPG), 4) produce a short README explaining filters.
Olivia Chen: Auditor also asked for proof that KMS keys haven't been rotated in that window (or show rotation events). Can we include key metadata snapshot?
Ethan Park: Yes — we'll export `GetKeyRotationStatus`, `DescribeKey` snapshots and include key policy versions. No plaintext key material, just metadata.
AuditorBot: Also request: include sample decryption request trace that ties a requestId to a service account and to the RBAC role at the time. Minimal sample size (3-5) is fine.
Maria Gomez: I'll pick 3 representative traces that show: service-account -> rolebinding -> Decrypt event. Will keep sensitive fields hashed.
Samir Patel: We'll produce a presigned S3 link to a zipped bundle and put the manifest in `bundle/MANIFEST.json` and README in `bundle/README.md`. We'll include file hashes like: `rbac.csv: sha256:...`, `kms_events.ndjson: sha256:...`.
Olivia Chen: Timeline? Auditor expects delivery EOD Friday. Can we make that?
Maria Gomez: I can run the queries tonight and start the packaging tomorrow morning.
Ethan Park: I'll export KMS metadata and GPG-sign the manifest once Maria uploads. Use key `sec-audit@redwood` for signature.
Samir Patel: I'll review the bundle and run an internal audit checklist, then create a short mapping doc: change -> PR -> approver -> timestamp -> related KMS event ids.
Olivia Chen: Thanks. One more thing — auditor asked whether we can provide live verification: a short walkthrough call where we show logs in Splunk with the filtered query. Are folks available for a 30m session on Friday?
Maria Gomez: I can do 10–11am PT.
Ethan Park: 10–11am PT works for me.
Samir Patel: I'm good at 10:30.
Olivia Chen: Great — I'll schedule 10:30–11:00 PT and confirm with the auditor.
AuditorBot: Received. Please attach the manifest hash to the calendar invite once available.
Olivia Chen: Will do. I'll post the presigned link and manifest hash in this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: Noted — FYI we'll exclude any entries with user->customer data by default; if auditor needs deeper samples they need LOA.
Olivia Chen: Good call. Thanks team — update here when uploads are live.
